query: How will you implement the leave-one-out shift-share instrument in code (exact aggregation steps) and which formal tests will you run to detect correlation between shares and local omitted shocks?

response.query: How will you implement the leave-one-out shift-share instrument in code (exact aggregation steps) and which formal tests will you run to detect correlation between shares and local omitted shocks?
response.answer: Implement leave-one-out shift-share by iteratively excluding one market, calculating market shares, and comparing to aggregate. Use correlation tests like Pearson's r to detect relationships between shares and local shocks.
